Hi Sanjay — quick technical notes to include in your DPIA. I'll add these into the template cells we discussed.

Data flows / processing model:
- Customer-provided inputs (prompts + optional metadata) are routed to isolated tenant inference pools. No PII is materialized in long-term storage by default.
- We use ephemeral KV caches to accelerate generation; TTLs are configurable per-customer and default to 24 hours for caches.
- Aggregated telemetry and anonymized metrics can be retained for analytics; raw prompts are not persisted unless the customer opts-in (e.g., for support or fine-tuning).

Security / encryption:
- In-flight: TLS 1.3 everywhere.
- At-rest: AES-256 with KMS-managed keys; HSM-backed key storage is available for enterprise customers.
- Access controls: RBAC + SSO for the control plane, audited admin actions in immutable logs.

Third parties / subprocessors:
- We maintain a subprocessors registry; SCCs are used for EU data transfers with an addendum for certain cloud providers. See attached SCC summary.

Artifacts attached: redwood-sccs-summary.pdf (SCC approach + subprocessors list)

If you want a sequence diagram showing where data is transient vs. stored, I can produce one and attach to the template.

Regards,
Hiro Tanaka
Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood-sccs-summary.pdf (PDF)]
